mechanism_narrative: A declining trend in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% over the past 3 months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and payroll employment signals weak consumer demand, which typically results in lower corporate revenue growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and PAYEMS decline, or the interaction effect (measured by the product term in a regression) has a Rank IC below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL above 2.5% year-over-year), a rising federal funds rate signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% and FEDFUNDS is rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 110.0 (index 2017=100) over the past 3 months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which typically leads to reduced corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO falls below 110.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index above 2.5% year-over-year signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to reduced real consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE above 4.5%), a further increase in unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over the past month signals deepening labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% and rises by more than 0.3pp in a month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A declining trend in real sales (RSAFS) over the past 6 months indicates weakening business demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS has declined over the prior 6 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
